meta.description: Download genome assemblies, gene records, and ortholog data from NCBI using the modern Datasets v2 CLI (replaces assembly_summary.txt scraping and many EFetch workflows). Use when bulk-pulling genome assemblies, gene metadata across species, ortholog sets, or BLAST databases; when E-utilities are too slow for genome-scale work; or when automatic checksum verification, parallel download, and clean accession-driven retrieval are required.

scientific_integrity.detail: Every value checked across all 10 inputs (organism names, lengths, gene IDs, ortholog counts, assembly stats, release dates) traced to real, live NCBI Datasets API responses on CLI 18.37.0; no fabricated accessions, counts, or metadata observed anywhere, including in the two wholly new workflows exercised (virus download, Insecta ortholog set).

practice_boundaries.detail: Not applicable in practice -- this Skill retrieves public genome/gene database records only; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or patient-level content is produced or possible via this CLI.

methodological_ground.detail: No statistical or causal claims are made. The ortholog-set caveat (one representative per species, not tree-reconciled orthology) remains accurately stated in both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md.

code_usability.detail: All 3 shipped example scripts (gene_metadata.sh, download_genome.sh, bulk_dehydrated.sh) now run unmodified against the installed CLI (18.37.0) and produce correct output -- confirmed by direct execution, not inspection. This reverses the pre-fix veto-adjacent finding (Code Usability was PASS pre-fix too, but only because the CLI itself worked while the Skill's own scripts failed; now both the CLI and the Skill's scripts work).

functional_suitability.note: Genome/gene/ortholog/virus/dehydrate-rehydrate workflows all verified correct on live re-run, including two workflows (virus download, Insecta ortholog set) beyond the fixer's own tests. -1 for the newly found rehydrate-verification gap (see reliability) not yet reflected in the doc's 'Checksum verification (automatic)' claim.

reliability.note: The aria2c filename-corruption P1 is genuinely fixed (awk $2->$3 plus a fail-loud sanity check, verified on 2 fresh species the fixer never tried) and the not-found case is now documented. NEW finding: `datasets rehydrate` -- the script's own documented 'Step 3: verify' safety net and SKILL.md's 'Checksum verification (automatic)' claim -- does not actually verify pre-existing files at all (confirmed twice: via a live NCBI bot-block that silently wrote an HTML error page as 'real' data, and via manual byte corruption against the tool's own recorded expected file size). This is a real, reproducible gap in the documented safety net for the exact bulk/HPC pattern the Skill recommends, not introduced by this fix but not caught by it either.

performance_context.note: usage-guide.md's redundancy pass (Prerequisites/8-step summary/Tips removed, all facts preserved once in SKILL.md) reduces token cost further without losing coverage; dehydrated-first guidance remains genuinely efficient.

agent_usability.note: All four live failures from the pre-fix audit (taxon-level gene query, two field-name sets, bare --ortholog) are gone; an agent following SKILL.md's code patterns verbatim now succeeds on every documented pattern tested, including on genes/clades the fix was never explicitly verified against (TP53, Insecta). -2 because the new rehydrate-verification gap is not yet reflected in Failure Modes/Common Errors.

human_usability.note: Error messages remain mostly clear; the two previously-misleading cases (silent zero-count, bare --ortholog) are now both documented in Common errors, so an agent hitting them has a path forward even though the CLI's own messages are unchanged.

security.note: Unchanged from pre-fix: consistent shell-variable quoting, no hardcoded secrets, --api-key documented only as an inline argument.

maintainability.note: All 3 example scripts now run unmodified against the pinned CLI version (Testability was the pre-fix weak point at 8/12); redundancy pass improved modularity by removing duplicated content between SKILL.md and usage-guide.md.

agent_specific.note: Escape-hatch table and composability remain strong and independently verified (still true: datasets download has no SRA subcommand); virus workflow -- named in the scope table but never tested by either the original audit or the fix -- also verified correct, broadening confidence in the doc's other scope claims.

inputs.label: Does `datasets rehydrate` actually verify pre-existing/corrupted files, as SKILL.md and bulk_dehydrated.sh's own Step 3 comment claim?
inputs.note: NEW DEFECT, not part of the fixer's 6 findings and not introduced by the fix. Reproduced twice: (1) a live NCBI bot-block during the WSL aria2c leg silently wrote the misuse.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov abuse-page HTML as if it were real genome data, and a subsequent `datasets rehydrate --directory .` reported 'All 3 files already rehydrated' without touching the corrupted files; (2) manually replaced a 373,156-byte genomic.gff (the tool's own dataset_catalog.json records this exact expected size) with a 50-byte placeholder string and re-ran rehydrate -- same 'already rehydrated' result, file untouched. rehydrate appears to check only file presence at the expected path, not size or checksum, despite SKILL.md's 'Checksum verification (automatic) ... Rehydrate workflows also verify' claim and bulk_dehydrated.sh's Step 3 comment ('datasets rehydrate validates checksums of all files').

assertions.text: datasets rehydrate runs without crashing on a directory with pre-existing files
assertions.note: Exits 0, prints a completion message, no crash.

assertions.text: rehydrate detects and re-fetches a file that is present but the wrong size (373,156 expected vs 50 actual, per its own catalog)
assertions.note: Reported 'already rehydrated'; file left unchanged at 50 bytes.

assertions.text: rehydrate detects and re-fetches a file corrupted by a real network failure (NCBI bot-block writing an HTML error page)
assertions.note: Same 'already rehydrated' result; the abuse.shtml HTML content was left in place under the real genome filename.

assertions.text: SKILL.md's 'Checksum verification (automatic)' claim holds for the documented aria2c + rehydrate HPC pattern
assertions.note: The claim is true for a clean, from-scratch rehydrate (verified in Inputs 3/5) but false for the compound pattern the Skill itself recommends as the bulk/HPC path (dehydrate -> aria2c parallel pull -> rehydrate 'to verify').

key_strengths: All 4 P1s and both P2s from the pre-fix audit are genuinely fixed, verified by live execution on data the fixer never tested: a second human gene (TP53), a second clade (Insecta), and two species the fixer's own aria2c/rehydrate tests didn't cover (Mycoplasma genitalium, Buchnera aphidicola).
The Python wrapper's camelCase -> snake_case field fix and the dataformat --fields corrections both hold against fresh live API responses, not just the fixer's own cached examples.
usage-guide.md's redundancy pass is real and clean: every fact it lost is present, correct, and non-duplicated in SKILL.md; no orphaned or contradictory claims found.

A genuinely new, previously-undetected defect was found and precisely characterized: `datasets rehydrate` does not verify pre-existing files against its own recorded expected size, silently undermining the documented safety net for the Skill's recommended bulk/HPC download pattern.

recommendations.title: `datasets rehydrate` does not verify pre-existing files -- 'Checksum verification (automatic)' claim is false for the documented aria2c + rehydrate pattern
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'Checksum verification (automatic)' section states 'Rehydrate workflows also verify. If a file fails checksum, Datasets retries up to 3 times then errors,' and bulk_dehydrated.sh's own Step 3 comment says 'datasets rehydrate validates checksums of all files.' Neither is true when the target file already exists at the expected path: `datasets rehydrate` reports 'All N files already rehydrated' without checking size or checksum, confirmed both via a real NCBI bot-block (aria2c wrote an HTML error page as if it were genome data) and via manual corruption against the tool's own recorded expected byte length in dataset_catalog.json.
recommendations.root_cause: `datasets rehydrate`'s local-state check appears to be presence-only (does a file exist at the expected relative path), not a size or checksum comparison against the values it itself records in dataset_catalog.json.uncompressedLengthBytes.
recommendations.fix: Add a step to bulk_dehydrated.sh (and a note in SKILL.md's Checksum verification section) that independently verifies file size against dataset_catalog.json's uncompressedLengthBytes (or re-downloads into a clean directory) after the aria2c leg, rather than trusting `datasets rehydrate`'s 'already rehydrated' report as a correctness signal. Downgrade the 'Rehydrate workflows also verify' claim to state this limitation explicitly.

recommendations.title: Virus download workflow has no worked code pattern
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's scope table names `datasets download virus` as in-scope, and the command works correctly when run, but there is no 'Code patterns' entry for it (unlike genome/gene), no --include guidance, and no dataformat virus-genome field example.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's worked examples focus on genome/gene; virus was likely added to the scope table without a matching code-pattern section.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'Download virus assemblies' code pattern alongside the existing genome/gene patterns, including a dataformat tsv virus-genome --fields example verified against a live --help catalog.
